facts.fact_text: On 21 September 2015 the applicant, together with Ms S., notified the Syktyvkar Town Administration of their intention to hold a 'picket' (пикетирование) on 25 September 2015 from 5 to 6 p.m.
The 'picket' notified on 21 September 2015 was intended to be held at the crossroads of Lenin and Kommunisticheskaya streets behind the Lenin monument in Syktyvkar.
The 'picket' notified on 21 September 2015 was expected to be attended by fifty people.
The stated aim of the 'picket' notified on 21 September 2015 was to 'discuss the arrest of the Komi Republic government'.
On 21 September 2015 the Syktyvkar Town Administration refused to approve the venue chosen by the applicant for the 'picket'.

The Syktyvkar Town Administration's refusal of 21 September 2015 pointed out that Komi Republic regional law no. 91-RZ of 20 November 2012 [sic] prohibited the holding of public events in Stefanovskaya Square.
The Syktyvkar Town Administration proposed that the 'picket' be held at one of the special locations for public events designated by the Komi Republic government.

Section 5 of Komi Republic Law no. 91-RZ of 29 November 2012 on the Holding of Public Events in the Komi Republic prohibits the holding of public events in Stefanovskaya Square in the town of Syktyvkar.

Section 5 of Komi Republic Law no. 91-RZ of 29 November 2012 on the Holding of Public Events in the Komi Republic prohibits the holding of public events at railway stations, bus stations, markets, airports, educational institutions, buildings of educational institutions, religious buildings and areas within a radius of fifty metres of the entrance to those facilities.

Section 5 of Komi Republic Law no. 91-RZ of 29 November 2012 on the Holding of Public Events in the Komi Republic prohibits the holding of public events at children's playgrounds, locations designated by the municipal authorities for children's recreation and activities, pedestrian pavements, bus stops, and public parking areas.

Section 5 of Komi Republic Law no. 91-RZ of 29 November 2012 on the Holding of Public Events in the Komi Republic prohibits the holding of public events at buildings in a state of disrepair and areas within a radius of fifty metres of the entrance to such buildings.

Section 5 of Komi Republic Law no. 91-RZ of 29 November 2012 on the Holding of Public Events in the Komi Republic prohibits the holding of public events at buildings under construction, reconstruction or repair and areas within a radius of fifty metres of the entrance to such buildings.

Section 5 of Komi Republic Law no. 91-RZ of 29 November 2012 on the Holding of Public Events in the Komi Republic prohibits the holding of public events at buildings occupied by the regional authorities of the Komi Republic, Komi Republic branches of the federal authorities, the municipal authorities of the Komi Republic, state institutions in the Komi Republic and areas within a radius of fifty metres of the entrance to those buildings.

Section 5 of Komi Republic Law no. 91-RZ of 29 November 2012 on the Holding of Public Events in the Komi Republic provides that the listed prohibitions apply in addition to the locations where the holding of public events is prohibited pursuant to section 8 paragraph 2 of the Federal Public Events Act.

Syktyvkar Town Administration's decree no. 9/3483 of 4 September 2013 described the perimeter of the zone in the immediate vicinity of the Constitutional Court of the Komi Republic where the holding of public events was prohibited.

The perimeter described in Syktyvkar Town Administration's decree no. 9/3483 of 4 September 2013 comprised the entire Stefanovskaya Square and the adjacent streets, including the area at the crossroads of Lenin and Kommunisticheskaya streets.

Syktyvkar Town Administration's decree no. 9/3483 of 4 September 2013 described the perimeter of the zone in the immediate vicinity of the Constitutional Court of the Komi Republic where the holding of public events was prohibited.

The perimeter described in Syktyvkar Town Administration's decree no. 9/3483 of 4 September 2013 comprised the entire Stefanovskaya Square and the adjacent streets, including the area at the crossroads of Lenin and Kommunisticheskaya streets.

The Syktyvkar Town Court noted in its judgment of 18 November 2015 that in accordance with the amended decree no. 10/4160 of 28 October 2008, it is prohibited to hold public events at the crossroads of Lenin and Kommunisticheskaya streets.

The Syktyvkar Town Court held in its judgment of 18 November 2015 that the Syktyvkar Town Administration's proposal to change the location of the applicant's public event was well reasoned and lawful.
The Syktyvkar Town Court held in its judgment of 18 November 2015 that the refusal to approve the location was lawful and acceptable.

The Syktyvkar Town Court held in its judgment of 18 November 2015 that the Syktyvkar Town Administration's decision of 21 September 2015 contained reasons justifying the impossibility of holding the public event at the chosen location, a well-reasoned proposal to change the location, and an explanation of the procedure for notifying public events.

The Syktyvkar Town Court held in its judgment of 18 November 2015 that the applicant was not deprived of a possibility to enjoy his constitutional right to hold public events in accordance with the procedure established by the Public Events Act.

The Syktyvkar Town Court held in its judgment of 18 November 2015 that the applicant's rights and freedoms under Articles 10 and 11 of the Convention were not restricted by the Syktyvkar Town Administration's contested decision of 21 September 2015.
The Syktyvkar Town Court held in its judgment of 18 November 2015 that there were no obstacles preventing the applicant from enjoying his constitutional rights.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the Syktyvkar Town Court rejected the complaint on the merits because the contested refusal to approve the chosen location of the picket had been made by the competent authority in accordance with the procedure prescribed by law.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the Syktyvkar Town Administration had given the applicant an objective possibility to enjoy his constitutional and Convention rights.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the Syktyvkar Town Court correctly applied the Public Events Act providing for the conditions for enjoying the right to peaceful assembly guaranteed by Article 31 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the Syktyvkar Town Administration's proposal to change the location of the public event chosen by the organisers had been substantiated, well reasoned and justified by the necessity to respect the balance of interests of the parties and to ensure public safety.
The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that it is prohibited to hold public events at the crossroads of Lenin and Kommunisticheskaya streets.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic noted in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that Decree no. 598 of 25 December 2012 by the Komi Republic Government designated special locations for holding political public events in Syktyvkar.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the choice of a location for an event and its approval by the municipal authorities does not restrict the participants' right to freedom of opinion and expression.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the applicant's argument that it was impossible to hold the event was hypothetical and did not refer to any valid reasons explaining why the locations proposed by the Syktyvkar Town Administration were incompatible with the public event's purposes.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that in accordance with Article 17 § 3 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, the enjoyment of one's rights and freedoms must not breach the rights and freedoms of others.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that there were objective and sufficient reasons for the proposal to change the location of the public event with the aim of ensuring a balance between the rights of the organisers and those of third persons.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the Syktyvkar Town Administration did not omit to examine the request for approval of the location of the public event and gave its reply to the applicant within the statutory time-limit.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the Syktyvkar Town Administration's reply contained reasons explaining why it was impossible to hold the public event at the chosen location and a well-reasoned proposal to change the location.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the applicant's constitutional rights and interests were respected and there was no violation of Article 11 of the Convention guaranteeing freedom of assembly, or of the Public Events Act.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the law does not guarantee the organiser of a public event an unconditional right to hold a public event at the location which he considers the most relevant to its political and social significance.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the Syktyvkar Town Administration fulfilled its statutory obligation to propose an alternative location for the public event that was compatible with its purposes.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the locations proposed by the Syktyvkar Town Administration were an adequate alternative to the chosen location and were in keeping with its purposes.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the arguments in the appeal submissions were based on an incorrect assessment of the facts of the case and an incorrect interpretation of the applicable legal provisions and did not therefore warrant the quashing of the Syktyvkar Town Court's judgment.

The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the Syktyvkar Town Administration's contested decision was in accordance with the Public Events Act, was made within the municipal authorities' powers and was in the interests of ensuring public order, with the aim of preventing disorder, protecting health and morality, and safeguarding the rights and freedoms of others.
The Supreme Court of the Komi Republic held in its judgment of 28 January 2016 that the Syktyvkar Town Administration's contested decision did not breach the applicant's rights.
